cr_data.provenance: The artist [1887-1986]; her estate; bequest 1987 to NGA. (Source: NGA, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Ptd. 1930." Series renumbered by O'Keeffe and Doris Bry in 1970. Pictured in 1931 and 1935 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photographs, see Appendix III, figures 43, 59. Included in 1934 New York (An American Place) as indicated in *Newark Evening News* (1934). Titled *Jack–in–the–Pulpit (Abstraction)* by Stieglitz on Abiquiú Notebooks photograph; reproduced and titled *Jack–in–the–Pulpit #7* in *America & Alfred Stieglitz* (1934); reproduced in *American Painting Today* (1939). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: Twisting, abstract maroon forms evoke the spathe and spadix of a jack-in-the-pulpit. The spathe-like form fills much of the canvas, curling in on itself to create a spiral pattern at the top of the image. Three spadix-like shapes stand one behind the other. The abstract plant form is framed by green, leaf-like shapes with streaks of pale blue.
